title: BBC Learning English from the News 2024 — Quiz 7
description: Choose the best answer for each question about vocabulary and usage.

elements.name: q61_disputed
elements.title: The ownership of the painting is disputed. What does “disputed” mean?
choices: People have agreed to share it.

elements.name: q62_isn_t_fooling_anyone
elements.title: “His excuse isn't fooling anyone.” What does the speaker mean?
choices: Nobody has heard the excuse yet.
Everybody thinks the excuse is funny.

elements.name: q63_upstart
elements.title: The established firms underestimated the upstart that quickly became a serious rival. Who was the upstart?
choices: A company that had left the market
A newcomer that rose quickly in importance
elements.correctAnswer: A newcomer that rose quickly in importance

elements.name: q64_drop_out
elements.title: Ana planned to run the marathon but dropped out after hurting her ankle. What did she do?

elements.name: q65_get_someone_s_nod
elements.title: The team needs to get the director's nod before hiring anyone. What does it need?

elements.name: q66_on_the_up
elements.title: “After a difficult year, business is on the up.” What does this mean?

elements.name: q67_outcast
elements.title: At the new school, he felt like an outcast. How did he feel?

elements.name: q68_staring_into_the_abyss
elements.title: With no money left and a deadline approaching, the organisation was staring into the abyss. What does the phrase suggest?
choices: It faced a grave and threatening situation.
It was looking back on a past mistake.
It had achieved its main goal.
It was waiting for a routine update.
elements.correctAnswer: It faced a grave and threatening situation.

elements.name: q69_2_0
elements.title: A team calls its redesigned training programme “Training 2.0”. What does the label suggest?
choices: It is a new and improved version.
It is only available to two people.
elements.correctAnswer: It is a new and improved version.

elements.name: q70_wake_up_call
elements.title: “The mock exam was a wake-up call. I needed to change my study routine.” What does “wake-up call” mean?
choices: A warning that made the speaker realise they needed to act
An invitation to take another exam
A telephone call that woke the speaker up
A reminder that the exam had been cancelled
elements.correctAnswer: A warning that made the speaker realise they needed to act
